comment: The one binder table of the program algebra (review log B17): which argument of which
constructor is elaborated under which additional binders. Everything that used to encode
this separately derives from it: `Node.binders`, `Node.closedChild` and `Node.childLevel`
(group Binders, src/Effect4/Program/Binders.lean) and the authoring lifts of every
constructor an author may write (group Authoring, src/Effect4/Program/Authoring/Lifts.lean).
`effTy` keeps the binder *types*; the agreement between the two is a theorem, not a copy.
A row names a constructor by its full name, the slots it binds in order, and for each of
its arguments in declaration order the slot indices in scope for that argument. `closed`
lists the arguments elaborated in the empty scope (a layer body). `whenHead` restricts a
row to the case where the constructor's first argument has that head (a statement list
extends the scope only after a binding yield). A constructor with no row binds nothing.
The profile (DI-84): constructors with no lift. `readerOnly` is the reader's canonical form
for generator code and the retiring invocation forms (`callback` is not one: an async row
authors as the reader reads it, through the generated row wrappers); `machineOnly` is what the printer
refuses as internal; `handWritten` is a name-resolving lift the core module writes itself.
`renames` gives a lift another name when the constructor's is a Lean keyword.
